clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move across the country in March 1952 and purchase of the orchard, within the year: June's homesickness and daily letters to her sister, Walter's long hours away from home, Glen's fights at his new school, Walter's cutoff from his brother over their father's land money, June's weeks in bed that first winter, Walter and June's rows over money for new trees, and June's turn toward the church choir and away from her letters by September 1953. The shifts pile up in the months after the move and settle as June finds her footing in the new place.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968 when the late frost took the whole crop and the bank called in the loan: Walter's heavy drinking, his and Glen's conflict over blame for the loan, Glen and Marian's overfunctioning as they took over the family's money and talks with the bank, Glen's son Roy's worsening asthma that winter, your bedwetting in the spring of 1969, your grandmother Ida's heart trouble found and her stop working at the bakery, and Walter's turn toward functioning as he stopped drinking and took pruning work by October 1969. The sale of the orchard in October 1968 sits in the middle of this time.

clusters.name: Glen's job lost at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen's job loss when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975: Glen's months out of work sitting in the truck in the yard, loud fights between Glen and Marian over money at night, Marian's overfunctioning as she took a second job cleaning offices, your loss of appetite and weight that summer, your distance from Marian as you kept to your room, Walter's return to drinking after six years, and your eating again and making the track team by June 1976. clusters.name: Wilma moving into Nora and Hollis's house, 1990–1991
